elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 15.9 is unchanged and still provides that the Agreement "will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA"; no New York choice of law is proposed (the drafter expressly targets the fallback).

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum language routes unresolved Disputes to "the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware", not to courts in New York County. The only New York reference that survives is the arbitral seat in Section 15.10.2.2, which is not a court forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 15.9 (untouched) selects "the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA", which is within the accepted fallback set; the retained federal-law overlay for Patents and Trademarks is pre-existing and does not displace Delaware law.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The new sentence in 15.10.1 does submit unresolved Disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction" of the Delaware state and federal courts, but the retained opening of Section 15.10.2.2 still reads "Any Dispute including the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be determined by the ICDR in accordance with its International Arbitration Rules" — an unqualified, mandatory arbitration mandate plus a competence-competence delegation that a party could invoke against the new court clause. The forum is therefore internally inconsistent rather than exclusively judicial.

reasons: Preferred level fails on both elements: Delaware law and Delaware courts are retained, so neither the New York choice of law nor New York County exclusive jurisdiction is achieved. That is acceptable only if the fallback is complete.
Fallback governing-law element is already met by untouched Section 15.9 (Delaware), and the drafter correctly left it alone.

Fallback forum element is not complete. Repair required in operative text: amend Section 15.10.2.2 so that it operates only where the Parties have agreed in writing under Section 15.10.2.1 (e.g. open with "Where the Parties have agreed in writing to arbitrate under Section 15.10.2.1, such Dispute...") and delete or subordinate the delegation of "the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate" to the ICDR. As rendered, the unqualified "Any Dispute ... shall be determined by the ICDR" sentence contradicts the new exclusive Delaware court submission and lets a party argue the tribunal, not the Delaware courts, decides whether arbitration applies.
The margin comment's assertion that "no contradictory arbitration right survives" is not borne out by the rendered language; do not rely on the comment to cure the retained 15.10.2.2 sentence.

Preserves intent fails for the same reason, and secondarily because the retained 15.10.1 sentence "no matters relating to breach or alleged breach of the ownership of intellectual property ... shall be resolved by arbitration, but rather shall be determined by a U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction" is now vestigial (there is no default arbitration to carve out from) and, read literally, keeps a merits forum broader than the Delaware courts. Consider recasting it as "shall be determined by the U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction" consistent with the Delaware submission, or leaving it but acknowledging the carve-out in the rationale.

Minimality is satisfied: only the forum sentence in 15.10.1 and the arbitration-initiation gate in 15.10.2.1 were touched; Section 15.9, the executive escalation period, the Section 7.5.5 Material Impact route and the preliminary injunctive relief carve-out (a permissible temporary-relief carve-out) are all retained without extras. Retaining the ICDR machinery as an opt-in is retention rather than an added requirement.
Not walk-away territory: the arbitral seat is New York (domestic), so the correct classification remains a medium-severity deviation on forum only.
